newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia says deal on Konkola Deep due next month.
newsitem.headline: Zambia says deal on Konkola Deep due next month.

text.p: Zambia's mines minister Christon Tembo said on Thursday a deal with a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa on the development of the Konkola Deep copper mine was expected next month.
"The final memorandum of understanding between the Zambian government and a consortium led by Anglo American Corp will be signed in February 1997," Tembo said in a statement to Zambia's parliament.
"This follows successful negotiations between the government and the consortium," he added.
Anglo, which has a 27.3 percent stake in Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines, which owns the mine, is looking to develop the giant mining area found in Zambia's Copperbelt province.

The project is seen as crucial to the future of the country's mining industry. The mine has proven reserves of 344 million metric tonnes of ore at 3.8 percent copper and is believed to have high potential for additional findings.
The consortium is expected to invest about $600 million to develop the project.
The consortium was due to have signed the memorandum with the government last year but later said it wanted to first conduct a feasibility study.
